prediction.title: drive past the measured CPU ceiling
prediction.injection: 8.0 req/s open-loop for 780s — M5-S4 measured 8 req/s at 101% of the 2-core limit
prediction.signature: latency and throttling with ZERO errors. Nothing crashes, nothing restarts, the route answers every request — and the service is nonetheless degraded by a factor of about six at the p50. A-6 is the only signal that can see it.
prediction.why: gotcha #74 as a prediction. M5-S4's ramp measured the throttled fraction at 0.23 / 0.51 / 0.79 / ~1.00 at 2/4/6/8 req/s with ZERO errors on every row, so at 8 req/s the fraction should sit above A-6's 0.90 bar and the rule fires after its 10m sustain — which is why the window is 780s and not the 180 s a latency measurement would need. A-1 is listed UNPREDICTABLE on purpose: it counts requests slower than 250 ms among status 200, and at saturation the p50 was 115 ms with an unmeasured tail. Predicting it either way would be a guess dressed as a derivation.
